bullets.title: Semis crater 28% in 22 days — worst rolling-month drawdown in decades as AI capex re-rates
bullets.body: The SOX semiconductor index fell ~28% over 22 days, one of its largest rolling-month drawdowns in history, driven by post-midterm concerns over data center build-out restrictions and a broader de-risking of crowded AI positions. NDX posted a 4-week losing streak including a ~6.4% single-day drop (worst since March 2020) that wiped ~$2.3T in Nasdaq cap. Semis now trade at 9–13x forward P/E — approaching or at 10-year median trough — while consumer staples trade at ~2x the multiple of the semi index, a 10+ year extreme.

bullets.title: AI capex narrative cracks: hyperscaler FCF turns negative, Texas/Ohio data-center moratoria emerge
bullets.body: Democratic midterm sweep — including governor wins in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, and New Mexico — created immediate regulatory overhang for data-center construction, with ~12–45 GW of planned 2028+ US capacity at risk per various broker estimates. Meanwhile, AMZN and GOOGL FCF turned negative ($35B and $9B respectively) in 3Q, reinforcing the 'prisoner's dilemma' capex thesis. AI capex grew 55% annualized last quarter and is expected to moderate to 20–30% in 2027; global AI capex is forecast at $1.68T in CY27 (+64% vs CY26), but proof of monetization is demanded before markets will re-rate.

bullets.title: Hedge fund capitulation: largest gross-leverage unwind since COVID, record put volumes, panic gauges spiking
bullets.body: HF gross leverage fell 5–6% in a single day on November 5 (5th largest decline since 2010), with nets at 42% (lowest decile vs 5-year history). Levered ETF rebalancing contributed ~$57–80B of supply; vol-targeting funds were estimated to sell a further $70–120B over the following week. Goldman's panic gauge hit 9.57/10 (3rd largest daily jump ever), VIX saw its 2nd-largest one-day spike ever (behind Feb 2018), and record 11M+ puts traded at CBOE. CNN Fear & Greed showed extreme fear; retail net selling on Nov 5 was a -5.7 standard-deviation event.

bullets.title: October jobs blowout (+165K vs +70K est.) locks in December Fed hike, kills dovish AHE deceleration thesis
bullets.body: October NFP surged to +165K with +84K in prior-month revisions, the strongest report in quite some time. White-collar hiring was the 2nd best monthly print since late 2022; the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% despite higher labor force participation; AHE reaccelerated to +0.37–0.4% m/m. Fed December hike probability jumped to 67–90% across street surveys. Core PCE is running 2.5–2.75% above the Fed's ~2% speed limit, and the disinflationary AHE deceleration narrative is now described as 'dead.'

bullets.title: Macro regime: two-speed economy — AI mid-cycle slowing, non-tech cyclicals early-cycle accelerating
bullets.body: A consistent cross-broker view emerged this week: tech/AI capex slowing from 80% to 50% YoY growth in 2027, while the other 90%+ of the economy is early-cycle, benefiting from the lagged impact of 2024–2025 Fed easing. Goods-producing jobs now outnumber tech jobs 10:1; real consumer spending targets 3% entering 2027; small business wage plans are elevated. Morgan Stanley pegged AI-related investment at 0.9pp of annualized 3Q GDP, up from 0.5pp in 2025. 22V calculates AI buildout contributes ~0.75pp to growth; a slowdown would drag only 40–50bp, well below recession threshold.

bullets.title: Post-midterm policy picture: Democrat Congress constrains AI regulation federally, state-level data-center pressure is real
bullets.body: Democratic congressional majorities (Senate ~54–55, House ~231+ seats) expand veto leverage over Trump on Iran, tariffs, and spending but are unlikely to pass sweeping federal AI restrictions — analysts note broad bipartisan consensus on AI safety/governance frameworks. The more immediate impact is at state level: Texas, Georgia, Ohio, NM, NV governors running on data-center moratoriums/conditions won, putting ~41% of planned US DC capacity in states with governors favoring pauses. The Turnberry Trade Truce (15% EU tariff ceiling) is now seen as more likely to hold, and Iran war resumption odds fell sharply.

bullets.title: Technical read: QQQs at COVID and late-2018 P/E lows; historical -5–6% single-day Nasdaq drops averaged +27% at 6mo
bullets.body: QQQ RSI fell below 30 for the first time since April 2025. Multiple technicians noted that -5–6% single-day Nasdaq declines have historically been followed by average gains of +27% at 6 months (100% hit rate since 1990, excluding dot-com era). SOX 14-day RSI hit 26, one of only two readings below that in the last decade. Ari Wald (Oppenheimer) upgraded Financial Services to Overweight, downgraded Energy; identifies current correction as episodic within a secular bull, noting a Russell 1000 Value/Growth breakout above two years of resistance. Jefferies expects choppy November through earnings season, with a re-grossing opportunity in early December.

bullets.title: Systematic and CTA selling still a headwind: ~$70–120B estimated equity supply over the week of Nov 9
bullets.body: CTAs flipped net short; Goldman and Nomura estimated ~$61–$135B of systematic selling over the 24–48 hours post the Thursday Nov-5 rout, with an additional ~$70–100B+ from vol-targeting strategies the following week. Dealer gamma was estimated negative through SPX 7000–7700 (SpotGamma). Volatility-target funds are estimated to have sold ~$80B equities in the week following the selloff. QDS (MS quant desk) models an initial bounce then renewed weakness before bottom, watching for correlation spike into 30s–40s.

bullets.title: Momentum factor crashed 40% from June peak — largest unwind in 40 years by JPM measure
bullets.body: The momentum factor declined ~40% from its June peak — including an 11% decline in October alone vs. the market's -5.8z — the largest unwind since post-GFC, per JPM global equity strategy. US TMT Momentum pairs down 70% from June highs, the biggest 1-year drawdown on record by a 17% margin. Semis most net-sold US theme, positioning back to early-2026 levels; global AI exposure fell quickly. JPM maintains its S&P 500 price target at 8,000 and recommends going long 12-month momentum (Semis/Tech Hardware) relative to 3-month momentum (Staples/Energy) into seasonally strong year-end.

bullets.title: Credit markets pricing AI risk: hyperscaler CDS doubled since March, $150B+ SPV-backed compute financing pipeline for 2027
bullets.body: Tech credit spreads have doubled since March, with hyperscaler 10y–30y curve flattening 9bps since Oct 20 as ORCL's $10B deal skipped the 30y tranche and META printed $15B vs. $25B+ expected. High-yield spreads widened 75bps since September start to a YTD high of 375bp. Over $150B of SPV-backed compute financing is announced for 2027 vs. ~$900M currently trading — a structural shift in AI financing — and spreads on that paper offer 100bp+ pickup to comparable unsecured debt. JPM forecasts a 25bp Fed hike in December; front-end yields are at risk of reversing higher if equities stabilize.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO roadshow — $1.25–1.75T valuation, compute costs approaching 90% of revenue by 2027
bullets.body: Anthropic is pressing ahead with its IPO, expected late November, targeting to raise $80–100B at a $1.25–1.75T valuation (down from prior ~$2T expectations). Anthropic's S-1 shows R&D vastly exceeds customer service costs, with compute expenses approaching 90% of revenue by Q1–Q2 2027 — a structural concern about commoditized intelligence with structurally low margins. 22V calculates Anthropic Q3 compute costs at $9.9B (+77% QoQ), 58% of revenue. AI labs face the risk of becoming low-margin commodity compute providers if prices keep falling.

bullets.title: Consumer bifurcated: Costco/WMT gaining share at the high end, lower-income household stress visible
bullets.body: Costco October US comps ex-gas accelerated to +8.1% (2-year trend +14.8%), partly driven by emergency preparedness stockpiling. Walmart grocery dollar share grew to ~20.3%, passing Kroger for #2. PSC Daily Consumer Confidence softened to 97.4 despite lower gasoline prices; a record 57% of consumers say high prices are eroding living standards. Lower-income-exposed restaurants and household goods companies (Wendy's, Papa John's, Clorox) cited pressured shoppers. High-end names (Marriott, Ralph Lauren, Tapestry) reporting solid demand. Holiday spending growth expected ~4–5%, driven primarily by pricing rather than unit demand.

bullets.title: Inflation risks asymmetric to upside: core PCE 50bp+ above target, ADP and JOLTS firming
bullets.body: September JOLTS surprised to the upside at 7.52M (vs 7.11M est.), quits rate bounced to 2.1% — the best since early 2025. Baseline core PCE forecasts for the next 3–4 months are described as 'too dovish' given tariff and cost pressures. Wolfe's 2027 macro forecast calls for core PCE peaking at 3.2% YoY end-2026, slowing to 2.5% by end-2027. Eurozone headline CPI hit 4.0% (cycle high) on energy. The BoE unanimously hiked 25bp and signaled at least one more. Riksbank hiked to 2.0%. Norges Bank held but kept December live.

bullets.title: Global DC capacity growth still compelling but new constraints: financing, inflation >10% YoY, powered land
bullets.body: Global data center capacity is forecast to grow from 136 GW in 2026 to 316 GW by 2030 (~20% CAGR). Goldman raised 2026/27/28 US DC construction spending forecasts to $80B/$100B/$125B; ~86 GW is already under construction. However, three-quarters of 2027 capacity is already under construction even as 41% of planned capacity sits in states where governors support moratoriums. Building cost inflation trending >10% YoY and tightening credit markets (AI-linked debt at $655B YTD heading toward $1T in 2027) are emerging as new structural headwinds alongside energy. EQIX and DLR are highlighted as beneficiaries of scarcity value from regulatory constraints.

bullets.title: Gold breaks $4,000 on safe-haven demand; copper caught between China supply tightness and AI demand risk
bullets.body: Gold rebounded ~3% post-election, breaking above $4,000/oz on lower US Treasury yields and softer oil prices (~$98/bbl Brent). JPM expects Fed to deliver only one more hike in December vs. market expectations, supporting gold upside above $4,500/oz in 2027. Copper is caught between Chinese social stocks near lower end of a 2-year range (~62kt) and post-election concerns about US AI buildout and tariffs; investor futures length halved since end-September. Oil collapsed following election results (down 13%+ on the week), driven by reduced Iran escalation risk — 2-year strip decline described as worse than 2008.

bullets.title: NVDA investigation: board opens probe after CEO Jensen Huang targeted by foreign intelligence effort
bullets.body: NVIDIA's board initiated an independent investigation after reporting that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Separately, the Financial Times reported NVIDIA instructed data-center clients to make the majority of their purchases to non-Chinese customers. The Commerce Department also reportedly cleared multiple Chinese firms to buy or assemble H200s despite sanctioned-entity ties.

bullets.title: Software sector: 89% EPS beat rate for 5 straight quarters but violent AI-driven price swings create L/S opportunity
bullets.body: Software EPS beat rate is stable at 89% for 5 consecutive quarters — well above historical median — with sales beats rebounding to 86.5% in 3Q26. Yet monthly return spread is 1.5x typical industry groups, and the Price Failure L/S strategy (short lowest quintile, long rest) returned +26% YTD with the lowest quintile down -23.4%. ServiceNow fell 27% the day after a narrow EPS miss; Fortinet fell 20% after a 100% EPS beat. Equity risk premium sits at 4.2% (below 50th percentile), leaving valuations volatile. The strategy works uniquely in software vs. the S&P 1500 (+6.6%).

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE $115B all-stock deal: strategic logic debated, Wolfe skeptical, deal termination risk ~38–62%
bullets.body: Marvell announced an all-stock acquisition of Lumentum at 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share (~$115B EV), aiming to combine silicon/DSPs with InP lasers/optical components for the scale-up and scale-in XPU adjacency. NVIDIA's Jensen Huang reportedly approved the deal before announcement. However, MRVL shares dropped ~28–32% post-announcement, pushing the implied premium into negative territory for LITE. Wolfe's special-sits analysis shows deals with >20% acquirer price declines have ~62% total event rate and ~38% termination rate — the largest such transaction has no historical precedent at this scale.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: defensives/value breaking out vs. cyclicals/growth for first time since 2001
bullets.body: Russell 1000 Value outperformed Growth by ~10pp in October, the widest spread since February 2001. Consumer staples (XLP) outperformed semiconductors by one of the largest 1-day moves in 10 years; XLP now trades ~2x the forward multiple of the semiconductor index. Housing stocks rallied sharply (LOW +740bp, HD +430bp) on peak-rate thesis. Financial Services upgraded to Overweight (Ari Wald, Oppenheimer). Defensives ex-Healthcare rebounded; AI-cyclical exposure fell quickly. Banks' 10-Q language on AI shifted from tailwind in 1H to credit/revenue risk concern by 3Q across C, GS, MS, MTB — Citi preferred at 8.6x 2028E EPS.
